title: Service-affecting inference event: customer bulletins and proof package
content:
Purpose
This doc is a compact customer-facing communication bundle for a service-affecting inference event (high latency + intermittent streaming truncation). It contains: 1) concise status page text variations for different severity windows, 2) an expanded customer bulletin for support and account teams, 3) a customer-focused mini-postmortem, and 4) a self-serve evidence & replay checklist customers can use to verify impact and recovery.

Goals and tone
- Transparent, non-technical-first but with enough technical detail for engineering contacts.
- Actionable — give customers steps they can take now and choices for recovery or replay.
- Respectful of SLAs; include compensation/credit language only when validated by SRE.

A. STATUS PAGE SNIPPETS (choose one by severity window)
1) Short: Initial detection (first 10–20 minutes)
Title: Degraded latency for inference requests in us-west-2
Severity: Partial degradation
Update: We’re investigating increased latency and intermittent truncated streaming responses for inference requests in us-west-2. Some requests may time out or return partial outputs. No data loss has been identified. Engineers are actively investigating. Next update in 30 minutes.
Suggested metadata: impact: "subset of requests in us-west-2"; affected-calls: "chat and streaming endpoints"; workaround: "retry on 429/timeout with jitter"

2) Medium: Ongoing (30–180 minutes)
Title: Degraded streaming responses — mitigation in progress
Severity: Ongoing degradation
Update: Our mitigation has reduced the rate of truncated streams but elevated latency persists for some requests. We have rolled a targeted routing rule that shifts new requests to healthy nodes; existing long-lived streams may still see truncation. If you see truncated outputs, retry the request. We will provide a targeted replay kit for impacted tenants after engineering completes request-level verification.
Next update: in 60 minutes or upon substantive change.

3) Recovery: Full verification
Title: Major latency incident resolved in us-west-2
Severity: Resolved
Update: The routing configuration that caused excessive queueing and KV-cache misses has been rolled back; latency and streaming behavior have returned to normal baselines. We are validating historical request integrity; affected customers will receive a tailored evidence package and replay guidance.

B. CUSTOMER BULLETIN (email / support note — for account teams to send to impacted customers)
Subject: Incident report: degraded inference latency and truncated streaming in us-west-2 (Sep 7–9, 2026)
Hi <Customer-Name/team>,
We wanted to update you about an event that may have affected your Redwood Inference traffic between 2026-09-07T13:04Z and 2026-09-09T05:22Z. Summary: for a subset of requests routed through our us-west-2 serving zone, customers saw elevated latency and occasional truncated streaming responses. No user data was lost or exposed.
What happened (customer-friendly): our runtime routing update introduced an unanticipated interaction with request batching and KV-cache retrievals. Under a specific workload shape (high concurrent short-chat sessions), some worker queues experienced unbounded queueing which increased latency and caused the stream to be cut short before final tokens were emitted.
What we did:
- Detected via SLO alert and prioritized incident response.
- Rolled back the routing change at 2026-09-08T23:16Z.
- Deployed a targeted hotfix to reduce KV-cache thrash and added a temporary routing isolation for latency-sensitive tenants.
- Replayed a curated subset of tenant traffic in an isolated verification cluster to confirm response integrity.
Customer impact:
- Impacted features: streaming chat and long-context generation (primarily streaming endpoints).
- Approximate fraction: ~2.3% of total request volume in the affected region.
- Observed failures: higher 95/99th percentile latency and truncated streams for some in-progress sessions.
Immediate guidance for customers:
- Retry truncated requests with exponential backoff (recommended max 2 retries).
- For streaming clients, subscribe to the event that signals finalization and, if missing, re-request the last chunk rather than re-sending the entire prompt.
- Contact support with a sample request-id (see evidence checklist below) if you need a per-request integrity check.
Next steps we’re taking:
- Full RCA and system-level remediation plan (see mini-postmortem).
- Per-tenant evidence packages and replay options. If you prefer a re-execution of affected requests (consent required), we will coordinate and present options for deterministic replay vs. best-effort re-generation.
Credits & SLA: we’re evaluating affected SLA windows and will propose credits where appropriate. If your team would like immediate escalation, reply to this message and we’ll prioritize a call.
Thanks for your patience — we’ll follow up with the formal postmortem within 14 days.

C. MINI-POSTMORTEM (customer-facing, concise)
1) Timeline (UTC)
- 2026-09-07T13:04 — SLO alerts began firing for us-west-2 latency and streaming error counts.
- 2026-09-07T13:22 — Incident declared; on-call SRE and serving runtime leads engaged.
- 2026-09-07T18:30 — Initial mitigations (throttle adjustments) reduced error rate by ~40%.
- 2026-09-08T00:12 — Routing change rolled forward (intended to reduce tail latency for general workloads).
- 2026-09-08T20:58 — Additional anomalies observed in KV-cache hit rates for the new routing; truncated streams increased.
- 2026-09-08T23:16 — Rollback of routing change; hotfix applied to KV cache eviction policy.
- 2026-09-09T05:22 — Metrics validated; incident moved to close and verification began.

2) Root cause (customer summary)
A follow-on routing change created a workload skew for a subset of GPU worker pools that amplified KV-cache misses. The combination increased per-request CPU scheduling and queue latency and resulted in streams being finalized prematurely under a time-based emission heuristic.

3) Immediate mitigation performed
- Rollback of routing rule.
- Hotfix improving cache retention for active prefixes.
- Temporary routing bypass for latency-sensitive routes.

4) Longer-term remediation planned
- Hardening routing rollout verification with a staged metric (cache hit ratio + stream-finalization rate) in addition to current latency SLOs.
- Fix driver-level scheduling to prevent queue build-up when the worker sees high short-session concurrency.
- New observability: token-level stream completion events instrumented and surfaced in console per-tenant.

5) How to verify for your team
- We will provide a per-tenant evidence ZIP containing: request-ids, timestamps, raw logs (redacted), and the replay transcript (if available). Use the replay checklist below.

D. CUSTOMER SELF-SERVE EVIDENCE & REPLAY CHECKLIST (for support ticket)
Please provide the following when you open a verification request (this lets us locate affected traffic quickly):
- sample request-id(s) (example format: r-0123abcd) or approximate time windows + tenant-id.
- route: e.g., v1/chat/stream or v1/generate.
- example prompt (if you can share); if not share input length and streaming config (max_tokens, stream chunk size).
Upon our validation we will deliver:
- A short log bundle (redacted) showing the worker that processed the request, start/end timestamps, and error/truncation flags.
- A replay artifact: deterministic replay for eligible calls or best-effort re-generation where determinism is not available.
- A short narrative: why this request behaved as it did and what we changed.
Customer choices for replay (consent required):
1) Deterministic replay: re-run the original inference path against the same model & weights; output will match original when cache state and random seeds are reconstructed. (Only possible for a small subset of cached requests.)
2) Best-effort re-run: generate a new response with current runtime — expected to be semantically similar but may differ token-for-token.
3) No replay: accept evidence bundle only.

E. TEMPLATE: SHORT INCIDENT CLOSURE NOTE (for public-facing closure)
Title: Incident resolved: streaming truncation and latency spikes in us-west-2 (Sep 7–9, 2026)\Body: The incident impacting streaming responses in us-west-2 has been resolved. The root cause was a routing change that increased cache misses and worker queueing for certain short-chat workloads. We rolled back the change and deployed a cache retention hotfix. We are providing affected customers with verification artifacts and replay options. For detail contact support or review the confluence incident page (confluence:infra/2026-09-inference-event-CAs).

F. SAMPLE SUPPORT SLR (internal note for CS to triage tickets fast)
- If customer reports truncated stream and request-id present -> mark priority P1 and route to incident-ops.
- If customer requests replay -> require signed consent form (templates attached) and estimate 48–72 hours for replay coordination.
- If customer requests credits -> collect usage windows and escalate to billing with RFC-INC-8421.

G. COMMUNICATION CHECKPOINTS & OWNERSHIP
- T+0–2h: detection + initial status page (SRE lead)
- T+2–8h: mitigation updates and customer bulletins (CS lead)
- T+24h: follow-up with impacted customers offering replay/evidence (CS + Infra)
- T+7–14d: full postmortem (public) with implemented remediation plan (eng leadership)

H. DRAFT: CUSTOMER-FACING VERIFICATION EMAIL (short version)
Subject: Verification and replay options for your impacted requests during Sep 7–9 incident\\nHi <name>,\\nWe identified requests for your tenant that were affected by the Sep 7–9 latency event. We can provide a replay (deterministic or best-effort) or a verification bundle with logs and timestamps. Reply with the option you prefer and 3 windows when we can schedule a short alignment call.\\nThanks,\\nAisha (on behalf of Customer Success & Infra)

Notes & next actions (internal):
- Finalize evidence package generation runbook and consents (owner: Marco Liu).
- Add token-level stream finalization events to per-tenant console (owner: Serving Runtime team).
- Prepare standard credit wording (billing) and template for common SLA outcomes (owner: Billing ops).

Document history
- 2026-09-07: initial draft for incident communications.
- 2026-09-08: expanded timeline and replay options.
- 2026-09-10: reviewed with SRE and product; updated mitigation language and added consent flow.

END
